subject.title: [Security] CSRF risk via dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback on network-exposed gateway (V-02)

question: Should OpenClaw keep Host-header origin fallback as a dangerous break-glass mode with extra safeguards, or remove/migrate it entirely?
rationale: The source disproves the simplest mismatched-Origin exploit but confirms a deliberate DNS-rebinding-hardening downgrade, and removing it affects a documented config path.

options.title: Keep And Harden
options.body: Preserve the explicit dangerous flag while adding focused Sec-Fetch/origin regression coverage, docs/audit clarity, and any low-risk runtime defense maintainers approve.

options.title: Remove With Migration
options.body: Delete the fallback and add a doctor/config migration path for users who relied on it, accepting the compatibility break as a security decision.

options.title: Accept Current Model
options.body: Leave the existing warning/audit behavior as the supported operator-controlled risk and close only after maintainers explicitly accept that policy.

recommendation.title: Keep And Harden
recommendation.body: Preserve the explicit dangerous flag while adding focused Sec-Fetch/origin regression coverage, docs/audit clarity, and any low-risk runtime defense maintainers approve.

likelyOwner.reason: The fallback and adjacent hardening history most directly route through steipete's gateway/security commits.
